steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Editing is the process of selecting, arranging and combining shots to construct narrative, meaning and emotional impact.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Continuity editing creates a seamless, invisible flow that maintains spatial and temporal coherence for the viewer.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The 180-degree rule ensures the camera stays on one side of an imaginary line between characters to preserve screen direction and spatial consistency.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Shot-reverse-shot alternates between two characters in conversation, creating the impression of a natural conversational exchange.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always name the editing technique precisely — 'dissolve' not 'a gradual change', 'match on action' not 'a smooth cut'. Explain the effect of each editing choice on the audience, not just what the technique is. Consider how editing pace changes within a sequence and what that shift communicates. Link editing to narrative: how do editing choices advance the story, create suspense or reveal information? Remember that editing is the one film language element that is entirely constructed — it does not exist in front of the camera.
